beats.lead: In a dark lab in New York
beats.text: Three people caught single photons with their bare eyes.
beats.note: Not a faint flash; one indivisible particle of light, produced by a quantum source built specifically to guarantee it was really only one.

beats.name: Alipasha Vaziri
beats.role: Rockefeller University. His team ran the test more than 30,000 times, because a signal this faint needed that many trials to prove it was not noise.

beats.context: How many times the experiment repeated before the result cleared random chance. That is the cost of proving something this faint is real.

beats.text: One photon primes the eye for the next.
beats.note: Detecting a photon made a second, unrelated photon easier to spot for several seconds afterwards, far longer than the retina's known response window, and still unexplained.

beats.text: The eye's near-total blindness to light this faint was known since the 1940s. Proving it could see the absolute floor took until 2016.

beats.line: The dimmest possible flash. Confirmed, not assumed.
